data.name: tools_sharetext_why_title
data.value: Why not just paste it in chat

data.name: tools_sharetext_why_1
data.value: Chat apps wrap long lines, eat indentation, and truncate walls of output.

data.name: tools_sharetext_why_2
data.value: A link expires; a chat message sits in someone's history forever.

data.name: tools_sharetext_why_3
data.value: The content is encrypted in your browser — the server stores bytes it cannot read.

data.name: tools_sharetext_uses_body
data.value: Error logs and stack traces, a config file someone needs to copy verbatim, meeting notes, a long URL list, or any text that is too big for a message box and too small to deserve a document.

data.name: tools_clipboard_what_body
data.value: An online clipboard moves text and images between devices that do not share a clipboard — a work laptop and a personal phone, a remote desktop and the machine in front of you, a colleague on the other side of a chat window. Press Ctrl+V here and the content is uploaded, encrypted in your browser, and turned into a link you can send anywhere.

data.name: tools_clipboard_why_1
data.value: Encrypted in the browser. The key lives in the link fragment and never reaches our servers.

data.name: tools_clipboard_why_2
data.value: It expires. Links auto-delete, so an old paste cannot leak months later.

data.name: tools_clipboard_why_3
data.value: Text reads inline. Small snippets render on the download page with a copy button — no file to open.

data.name: tools_clipboard_why_4
data.value: No account. Paste, copy the link, done.

data.name: tools_clipboard_good_body
data.value: Sending a stack trace to someone without mangling it in chat. Getting a screenshot off a locked-down work machine. Moving a config snippet, an SSH key you are about to rotate, or a wall of log output that a messaging app would truncate.

data.name: tools_images_why_title
data.value: Why images sent through chat go blurry

data.name: tools_images_why_body
data.value: Messaging apps compress images to save bandwidth: they lower resolution, degrade JPEG quality, and strip EXIF data. Screenshots with text show it most — blurry glyphs, jagged edges. With photos of documents, drawings, or camera shots, what is lost can never be recovered.

data.name: tools_images_how_body
data.value: Paste an image (Ctrl+V) or drag a file onto the send page. The file is encrypted right in the browser, then uploaded directly — no compression step. The receiver opens the link and downloads the exact original file — same size, same quality, EXIF intact if the image has it.

data.name: tools_images_diff_1
data.value: No compression, no format conversion. PNG stays PNG, RAW stays RAW.

data.name: tools_images_diff_2
data.value: End-to-end encryption. The key lives in the link; the server cannot read the content.

data.name: tools_images_diff_3
data.value: Links auto-expire. Images do not linger on the internet indefinitely.

data.name: tools_images_diff_4
data.value: No account needed. Paste, copy the link, send.

data.name: dpa_subtitle
data.value: The controller–processor terms under which QuickShareCloud handles personal data on your behalf, per GDPR Article 28.

data.name: dpa_s1_body
data.value: You are the data controller. QuickShareCloud is the processor, and processes personal data only on your documented instructions — which, in practice, are the actions you take in the product.

data.name: dpa_s2_body
data.value: Processing covers the files you upload and the account and recipient data attached to them, for as long as your account is active plus the retention window you configure. Deleting a delivery deletes its stored bytes; deleting your account removes the rest.

data.name: dpa_s3_body
data.value: Encryption in transit and at rest, per-link access controls (password, one-time code, IP and country rules), hashed IP addresses, an append-only audit trail, and least-privilege access for our own staff. The current control map is published on the SOC 2 readiness page.

data.name: dpa_s4_body
data.value: Cloudflare R2 (object storage), our email delivery provider, and PayOS (payments). We will give notice before adding a sub-processor that handles your content.

data.name: dpa_s5_title
data.value: 5. Data subject rights and breach notice

data.name: dpa_s5_body
data.value: Export and erasure are self-service from your account. We will notify you without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal-data breach affecting your data, with what we know at the time.

data.name: dpa_s6_body
data.value: Storage region selection is not yet available; content is stored in our default region. If your obligations require a specific region, tell us before you sign.

data.name: dpa_sign_login
data.value: Sign in to countersign this agreement against your account.

data.name: dpa_resign
data.value: You signed version {0}. The current terms are version {1} — countersign again to accept them.

data.name: dpa_not_legal_advice
data.value: This page is the agreement and the record of your signature. It is not legal advice; have your counsel review it as you would any contract.

data.name: soc2_subtitle
data.value: Where we actually stand against the Trust Services Criteria, control by control.

data.name: soc2_not_certified
data.value: QuickShareCloud is not SOC 2 certified. No audit has been performed and no report exists. This page is a readiness map, published so a vendor review can see the real position rather than a marketing one.

data.name: soc2_cc61_how
data.value: OAuth sign-in, workspace roles, per-seat provisioning and revocation. Enterprise SSO and SCIM are not built yet.

data.name: soc2_cc62_how
data.value: Seat revocation is immediate and restores the member's own plan; account deletion purges content and cascades its records.

data.name: soc2_cc66_how
data.value: TLS everywhere, security headers and CSP, per-delivery IP allowlist and country rules evaluated fail-closed.

data.name: soc2_cc67
data.value: Data in transit and at rest

data.name: soc2_cc67_how
data.value: HTTPS in transit, encrypted object storage, client-side AES-GCM for end-to-end deliveries, hashed IPs and hashed tokens at rest.

data.name: soc2_cc72_how
data.value: Append-only security timeline per account and per workspace, 90-day retention, cross-tenant access attempts recorded.

data.name: soc2_cc73_how
data.value: New-device alerts, quota threshold alerts, error tracking, and audit streaming to your SIEM. There is no formal on-call rotation or documented incident response runbook.

data.name: soc2_cc81_how
data.value: Version control, automated test suite and CI on every change, feature flags for staged rollout. Change approvals are not independently evidenced.

data.name: soc2_a12_how
data.value: Managed object storage with provider-level durability, automated database and object backups, public status page. Restore has not been exercised on a schedule with retained evidence.

data.name: soc2_c11_how
data.value: Workspace-scoped queries on every read, legal hold, retention policy, and right-to-erasure with byte-level purge.

data.name: soc2_p42_how
data.value: Per-account retention policy, per-delivery expiry, trash grace period and sweeps that delete stored bytes rather than just rows.

data.name: soc2_gaps_body
data.value: These are the items an auditor would raise first. They are open issues, not oversights we are hoping nobody notices.

data.name: soc2_gap_pentest
data.value: No annual third-party penetration test on record.

data.name: soc2_gap_policies
data.value: Internal policy set (access control, incident response, vendor management, security training) is not written down.

data.name: soc2_gap_drtest
data.value: Backup restore is automated but not exercised on a schedule with retained evidence.

data.name: soc2_gap_vendor
data.value: No formal sub-processor review or vendor risk assessment process.

data.name: soc2_gap_auditor
data.value: No auditor engaged and no observation window started.

data.value: Phase 1 — close the evidence gaps: write the policy set, schedule a restore drill, run a penetration test.

data.name: soc2_phase2

data.value: Phase 3 — engage an auditor, agree scope, and begin the Type II observation window.
